To obtain probabilistic results, the framework applied CP with different variants, such as Mondrian Binning (MB) and Conformal Predictive System (CPS), to enhance the reliability of prediction intervals. To address the arbitrary bin count in CP with MB, the paper proposes a novel CP variant, namely: Adaptive Mondrian Binning (AMB). Its performance, along with other CP methods, is evaluated and benchmarked against quantile regression methods on two actual datasets from the region of Amsterdam, the Netherlands, and Sydney, Australia. Results show that using LightGBM as the deterministic regressor, AMB outperforms quantile regression and other CP variants. The generalizability of the proposed framework is analysed for both probabilistic outputs and key sub-processes, such as deterministic disaggregation and capacity estimation.

title: Multi-Time Scale Distributed Stochastic Economic Dispatch for Flexible Traction Power Supply System
abstract: Flexible traction power supply system (FTPSS), integrated with renewable energy, energy storage, and power flow controllers (PFC), offers great potential for safe and economical railway operation. However, the uncertainty in traction load and photovoltaic (PV) output poses significant challenges to cost-effective dispatch. Therefore, a multi-time scale distributed stochastic economic dispatch method for FTPSS is proposed. The prediction module uses LSTM to produce point forecasts, while KDE models the forecast errors to construct predictive intervals and generate scenarios for PV output and traction load. A stochastic programming model is then formulated, where uncertainties in traction load and PV are represented by chance constraints and scenarios. In the first stage, the day-ahead forecast is used to solve the stochastic optimization model to minimize daily operational cost. In the second stage, the scheduler uses the day-ahead plan as a soft reference and re-optimizes at each rolling step with updated probabilistic forecasts, implementing only the first control move to maintain real-time responsiveness and economic efficiency. The optimization model is solved using an ADMM-based distributed algorithm, which accounts for limited inter-subsystem communication and reduces computational complexity. A case study based on a real electrified railway demonstrates that the proposed method improves economic performance by reducing operating costs by approximately 9% under uncertainty.

title: Dynamic Behavior Modeling of Price-Responsive Flexible Loads: A Deep Learning-Parameterized Inverse Optimization Approach
abstract: Accurately modeling the behavior of price-responsive flexible loads (PRFLs) is increasingly critical for enhancing power system flexibility. While existing inverse optimization methods can achieve flexible load modeling using only external price-response data, the surrogate model with time-invariant parameters severely limits its ability to capture dynamic behaviors induced by user demands, weather conditions, etc. In contrast to mainstream static modeling formulations, this paper proposes a Deep Learning-parameterized Inverse Optimization (DL-IO) method that enables dynamic surrogate modeling of PRFLs. Specifically, a dynamic virtual energy storage (DVES) model is formulated as the surrogate model, with its parameters represented by multi-task deep learning to exhibit time-varying properties. Then, the DVES model is integrated into the DL-IO framework, enabling the approximation of response behaviors for thermostatically controlled loads (TCLs) and electric vehicles (EVs) based solely on price-response data and public information. To solve the resulting bi-level DL-IO problem, it is reformulated as an empirical risk minimization task, which consists of a deep learning-based parameter estimation layer and an optimization-based response estimation layer. An analytical end-to-end gradient is then derived and backpropagated through both layers to achieve behavior learning. Numerical tests indicate that the proposed modeling method outperforms existing inverse optimization and data-driven regression approaches.

title: A Cross-Line Successive Fault Detection of Distribution Network Based on Zero-Sequence Capacitance Variation
abstract: In non-effectively grounded system, the rise in phase voltage during single-phase grounding (SPG) fault poses a significant threat to the system’s insulation integrity. The increasing cabling rate in distribution network has led to a rising proportion of cross-line double successive single-phase grounding (SSPG) faults triggered by initial fault. To address the challenges of weak characteristic and difficult detection of such successive fault, this paper proposes a SSPG detection method based on zero-sequence capacitance variation. First, the dynamic zero-sequence equivalent network during successive faults is simplified, and derive the zero-sequence current (ZSC) expressions for each feeder under both overdamped and underdamped conditions. Subsequently, the singular value decomposition-total least squares extended Prony algorithm is employed to fit the zero-sequence voltage (ZSV) and ZSC, enabling the calculation of zero-sequence capacitance for both initial and successive faults in the complex frequency domain. A detection criterion is then constructed using the variation of capacitance. Finally, digital simulations and recorded field data validate the correctness and feasibility of the theoretical analysis.

title: Spatial-Constrained Structure Optimization of the Mover for Minimizing Power Consumption in Maglev Planar Motors
abstract: This paper presents a novel spatial-structure optimization method for the coils of moving-coil magnetically levitated planar motors (MLPMs) to address the coupled challenges of power consumption and spatial constraints. The proposed framework systematically determines the optimal coil geometry and arrangement to minimize power consumption under a required force output and a strictly confined mover volume. A harmonic-based electromagnetic force model is employed to guide a compact coil layout by defining the number, length, and spacing of coils. These parameters are subsequently incorporated into a power-minimization model to determine the coil and beam widths. A final trade-off optimization is performed to balance high-order harmonic suppression and manufacturing tolerance, resulting in a comprehensive design strategy. Experimental results validate the superiority of the proposed method: under identical motor dimensions and magnetic pole pitch, the optimized design achieves more than a 40% increase in thrust-to-weight ratio (TWR) while reducing thrust fluctuation to below 15%. Furthermore, at a constant levitation height, the proposed design reduces power consumption by 10% to 25% compared with conventional systems. These findings demonstrate significant improvements in system stability and force efficiency, offering a generalized and practical design guideline for high-performance moving-coil MLPM.

title: Impact of Shielding Configurations With Magnetic-Electrically Conductive Alloy on Multi-Physical Fields in the End Region of Air-Cooled Synchronous Condenser
abstract: In large-capacity air-cooled synchronous condensers (ACSCs) operating under deep leading-phase conditions, significant end leakage flux induces substantial losses and heating in the stator end components. Effective electromagnetic shielding is therefore a critical design consideration and a novel shielding configuration utilizing magnetic-electrical conductive alloys is proposed in this article. Using a 300 MVar ACSC as a case study, the three-dimensional transient electromagnetic field model of the end region is first established. The effects of four configurations (copper shield+magnetic shield, Fe-16<inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\%$</tex-math></inline-formula>Cu alloy shield+magnetic shield, single Fe-20<inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\%$</tex-math></inline-formula>Cu alloy shield, and single magnetic shield) on the leakage flux density and losses in end components are analyzed. Subsequently, a global ventilation network and a fluid-thermal coupling model for the end region are developed for each configuration. The results from network and aforementioned losses serve as boundary conditions for the fluid-thermal coupling model. The flow fields and the temperature distributions under different configurations are then determined. The findings demonstrate that each shielding configuration exhibits specific advantages and limitations. Experimental validation based on traditional scheme confirms the accuracy of the model and methodology. The simulation results elucidate the significant potential of the Fe-Cu alloy. The single Fe-20<inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\%$</tex-math></inline-formula>Cu configuration reduces the hot-spot temperature of shield, and significantly lowers weight and cost while effectively protecting the end iron core.

title: Stage-Wise Analytical Modeling of the Stray Magnetic Field in Surface-Mounted Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors Under Mixed Eccentricity
abstract: Conventional subdomain methods face challenges in calculating the stray magnetic field of surface-mounted permanent magnet synchronous motors (SPMSMs) under eccentric conditions due to their inability to handle complex boundaries, leading to low computational efficiency. To address these issues, this paper proposes a cell-based Schwarz-Christoffel (SC) mapping method and a stage-wise calculation strategy to improve computational efficiency while maintaining accuracy. First, an analytical model (AM) integrating equivalent surface current, conformal transformation method is established. Based on magnetic field superposition, the load air-gap magnetic field is derived. Second, a stage-wise subdomain-based computational strategy is employed to decouple the magnetic field calculations for the air-gap region and the outer air region. The stray magnetic field is analytically modeled using SC mapping and separation of variables. Finally, the proposed method is validated through experiments on an 8-pole 18-slot interior-rotor SPMSM with mixed eccentricity. Results show that the TM achieves a computational error of only 3.49% and that the computational speed is 136 times faster than that of the finite element method (FEM).

title: Sensorless Control of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors Using Model Predictive Algorithm Based Back-EMF Observer
abstract: Back-electromotive force (back-EMF) based sensorless control is widely applied in permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) drives. For high-gain back-EMF observers, the control law often leads to an inherent trade-off between steady-state accuracy and dynamic response. To address this issue, a model predictive control (MPC)-based observer designed in discrete-time domain is proposed in this article. In the studied observer, the optimal control action selected from a predetermined set is adopted to eliminate the current estimation error. Then, the estimated back-EMFs can be extracted from the applied control actions. By leveraging traversing optimization, the proposed method improves the current error and observation accuracy while maintaining fast response and robustness. Experimental results conducted on a 1-kW PMSM platform verify the effectiveness of the proposed observer.

title: Dynamic Current Control Strategy of Grid-Connected Voltage Source Converters Feeding Constant Power Loads for Transient Stability Enhancement
abstract: The negative impedance characteristic of constant power loads (CPLs) can destabilize grid-connected voltage source converters (VSCs) by introducing positive feedback loops. To this end, this paper proposes a dynamic current control strategy for grid-connected VSCs with CPLs to enhance system transient synchronous stability (TSS). Firstly, a nonlinear phase-locked loop dynamic model is developed for VSCs. It explicitly incorporates the CPL impact, which indicates CPLs introduce coupling between the d-axis and q-axis components of VSC terminal voltage, and a positive feedback loop in VSC control scheme. Secondly, equal area criterion and phase-portrait analysis are used for qualitative and quantitative analysis to assess the CPL impact on TSS, respectively. The findings indicate the impact is related to the VSC output current. Therefore, a dynamic current control strategy for VSCs is proposed. It adds the current compensation term to neutralize CPL-induced destabilizing effects, guaranteeing the existence of stable equilibrium points that ensure both TSS and CPLs operation at rated power under grid faults. Meanwhile, a simple and fast VSC capacity calculation method is proposed. It can accurately calculate the required VSC capacity for achieving the above control objectives. Finally, simulation and experimental comparisons with existing methods verify the validity of the proposed strategy.

title: A Precise Nonlinear Eddy-Current Magnetic Network Model for the Analysis of Electromagnetic Buffer
abstract: In this paper, a precise nonlinear eddy-current magnetic network (PNEMN) model is proposed to analyze the performance of the cylindrical permanent magnet (PM) electromagnetic buffer (EB). In this EB, the permanent magnet is radially magnetized and separated by iron teeth. When the EB is working, intense eddy currents are induced, severely distorting the original magnetic field, so that conventional magnetic equivalent circuit (MEC) models can no longer provide an accurate solution. To solve this problem, this paper adopted refined magnetic reluctance elements and incorporated eddy currents into the magnetic network model, fully coupling them with the original magnetic field. The convergence of this method is discussed in detail. To make this model more comprehensive, nonlinear magnetic saturation, end effects, and slot effects have also been taken into account. Optimal computational efficiency is achieved by judiciously selecting boundary conditions. A finite element model and the experiments on a prototype were built to verify the accuracy of the proposed model. Finally, the operating characteristics of the eddy current brake are analyzed, and its critical speed is about 7.5 m/s.

title: Sliding-Mode Speed Control for Predictive-Torque-Control-Based Induction-Machine Drives Based on Adaptive-Variable-Rate Reaching Law and Disturbance-Extended Sliding-Mode Observer
abstract: For the predictive-torque-control (PTC) based induction-machine (IM) drives, to promote the speed tracking performance as well as the robustness against various unknown disturbances, such as friction, external load disturbance and parameter mismatch. A sliding-mode control with adaptive-variable-rate reaching law (SMC-AVRRL) and a disturbance-extended sliding-mode observer (DESMO) is proposed. First, the speed loop of PTC which utilizes the classical PI control is analyzed. It indicates that the control performance of the PI controller degrades apparently under sudden load disturbances and induction-machine parameters mismatch. Then the sliding-mode control with adaptive-variable-rate reaching law is proposed. Taking the typical reaching law, namely exponential reaching law (ERL), as a comparison object, the AVRRL method can reduce the chattering and convergence time simultaneously. The stability of the proposed SMC-AVRRL is analyzed by the Lyapunov stability theory. Moreover, to further enhance the anti-disturbance capacity, the proposed SMC-AVRRL is then combined with a disturbance-extended sliding-mode observer (DESMO), named the SMC-AVRRL + DESMO method. The experimental results show that the proposed SMC-AVRRL + DESMO method can not only achieve high speed tracking accuracy, but also achieves better robustness.

title: Pricing Appliance Usage Privacy for Enhancing Usability of Smart Meter Data
abstract: Consumers’ privacy concerns often limit the usage of their smart meter data in several data-driven applications. While privacy-preserving algorithms can address the privacy concerns of consumers, these algorithms erase useful information; thus reducing the data usability. Data usability can be enhanced if the utility can directly utilize the smart meter data of consumers without transforming the same using privacy-preserving algorithms. However, this is not possible unless consumers give up their privacy rights over their smart meter data. Offering monetary compensations to consumers can be a possible approach to encourage them to give up the privacy rights over their smart meter data. Hence, this paper proposes a novel privacy pricing method that monetarily compensates the loss of appliance usage privacy incurred by the consumers who agreed to give up the privacy rights over their smart meter data. At first, a consumer’s appliance usage privacy is modeled based on how the consumer’s consumptions fluctuate over a given time period. Then, a nonlinear convex optimization problem is proposed using the privacy model to determine the privacy prices of a set of consumers under a given budget of the utility. The properties of the optimal solution are demonstrated mathematically. It is shown that the practical implementation of the proposed pricing method is unlikely to impact the consumption patterns of consumers. The impacts of the utility’s budget and the number of participating consumers on the privacy prices are illustrated using practical smart meter data while considering heterogeneity in the privacy concerns of consumers. Further, a novel metric is proposed which shows that, unlike the existing pricing methods, the privacy prices generated by the proposed method are sufficient to address the privacy concerns of most of the participating consumers.

title: A Novel Magnetic Integrated Three-Phase EMI Filter for Differential-Mode and Common-Mode Interference Suppression in PMSM Drive Systems
abstract: The application of three-phase electromagnetic interference (EMI) filters in permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) drive systems can reduce common-mode (CM) interference while filtering out differential-mode (DM) interference in phase currents. Conventional filters will increase the volume and weight of the system. This article proposes a fully magnetic integrated three-phase EMI filter, with a magnetic core consisting of a toroid and a Y-branch limb. The toroid is primarily employed to concentrate the CM flux while providing the path for the DM flux. The Y-branch limb is used to carry the DM flux. The distribution of the flux in the proposed filter under different winding distribution patterns is analyzed. The DM and CM inductances are derived. The optimal winding distribution pattern is determined through quantitative and qualitative comparison. The magnetic saturation analysis is provided by deriving the maximum magnetic flux density of the proposed filter. The magnetic flux density of the proposed filter is verified through ANSYS simulation. The experiment is conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed filter. The results show that the proposed filter can significantly reduce the volume and weight of the system compared to the conventional filter under the same DM and CM suppression performance. In addition, a DC side EMI filter is manufactured to assess its impact on the electrical performance of the motor side. The results indicate that the DC side EMI filter cannot replace the proposed filter. The proposed filter can enhance the performance and reliability of the PMSM drive system.

title: Physics-Informed Series-Aware Graph Transformer Model for Net Load Forecasting
abstract: The growing integration of renewable energy sources (RESs), such as photovoltaic (PV) and wind (WD), has significantly increased the variability of net load (NL), posing critical challenges on the net load forecasting. In this paper, a novel physics-informed series-aware graph Transformer (PISAGT) model is proposed for the net load forecasting, which synergistically combines the advantages of both direct and indirect forecasting methods to achieve superior forecasting performance. Firstly, a physics-informed loss module (PILM) is proposed, which introduces the physical characteristics of the net load into the loss function to incorporate physical knowledge in the gradient descent optimization, thereby enhancing the model’s generalization capability for more stable and trustworthy predictions. Secondly, a variable-scale patch embedding method segments time series into subsequence-level patches and transforms them into 2D representations, which enables the forecast model to simultaneously capture local temporal patterns across diverse forecasting horizons. Thirdly, a series-aware graph learning mechanism (SAGLM) which includes graph token encoding, adaptive adjacency matrix learning, and graph convolution, is proposed to integrate graph neural networks (GNNs) with Transformer within a synergistic framework to comprehensively capture intra-series and inter-series dependencies in net load datasets. Finally, case studies on the real-world datasets demonstrate that the PISAGT model can achieve a 14.4% improvement in prediction accuracy compared with direct forecasting methods, showing its effectiveness in net load forecasting.

title: Adaptive Fault-Tolerant Control Based on Model-Free Predictive Current Control for PMSM With Dual Star-Delta Windings
abstract: This paper proposes a model-free predictive current control combined with an adaptive fault-tolerant control (AFTC-MFPCC) strategy for dual star-delta windings permanent magnet synchronous motor (DSDW-PMSM) under different phase shift angles. The proposed strategy enhances the operational performance of this motor when current sensor fault or open-phase fault occur in any star-connected winding phase, showing strong adaptability and robustness. Firstly, the invariance of the fundamental magnetomotive force (MMF) under single open-phase fault in DSDW-PMSM with different phase shift angles is analytically derived. Secondly, an adaptive fault-tolerant control strategy is proposed. Upon detecting a persistent zero current in any phase, it switches the adaptive fault-tolerant transformation matrix without explicit fault diagnosis, thereby avoiding the impact of current sensor faults and reducing the fault detection time. Subsequently, the xy-axis reference values are modified through current feedback, enabling the motor to adaptively transition from the fault state to the normal operation state. Furthermore, model-free predictive current control is employed to replace traditional PI control or deadbeat predictive current control in the current loop module of the vector control structure, which outputs four voltage vectors. This method avoids current tracking errors and severe waveform distortion caused by inaccuracies in motor parameter inputs. Finally, tests are conducted on a 24-slot/10-pole DSDW-PMSM with a 15° phase shift to validate the feasibility of the proposed method.

title: Multi-Stress Aging of Service-Aged and Backup Hydrogenerator Stator Coils Under Load Cycling
abstract: Frequent start–stops in hydrogenerators impose increased thermal, mechanical, and electrical stresses on stator winding insulation, accelerating degradation and potentially leading to failure. To emulate such operating conditions, a multi-stress, single-phase stator-slot model was built to cycle stator coils between 40 and 110 <inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$^{\circ }$</tex-math></inline-formula>C while simultaneously applying 1.5 times the rated phase-to-ground voltage (<inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">${U_{0}}$</tex-math></inline-formula>). Service-aged and backup coil groups taken from the same hydrogenerator were tested, with partial discharge (PD) recorded during cycling (on-cycle) and off-cycle diagnostics at room temperature, including PD inception voltage, PD measurements at 1.5 <inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$U_{0}$</tex-math></inline-formula>, and loss tangent. The on-cycle results show distinct aging trajectories: the service-aged coils entered a stable-degradation regime with limited, similar discharge magnitudes during heating and cooling, whereas the backup coils exhibited larger, more frequent discharges, with PD markedly higher during cooling than during heating at the same temperature. Off-cycle measurements indicate similar trends but with lower magnitudes, suggesting that room-temperature tests alone cannot probe multi-stress degradation. The study demonstrates that reliable assessment requires the use of combined on-cycle and off-cycle diagnostics under representative loading conditions.

title: Real-Time Reactive Power Limits of Synchronous Generators: Application to the New Spanish Voltage Control System
abstract: The voltage control of the Spanish transmission network faces growing challenges due to the high penetration of renewable energy sources, as evidenced by the Iberian Peninsula blackout on April 28, 2025. Synchronous generators have traditionally ensured voltage stability, but their role becomes even more critical in low-inertia systems with limited synchronous generation. This paper presents a real-time method for computing the reactive power limits of synchronous generators at the network connection point, aligned with the new Spanish voltage control system. The proposed approach determines maximum and minimum reactive power capabilities as functions of active power, network voltage, transformer tap position, and key generator constraints, including armature current, excitation system and stability limits, and admissible voltage ranges. Unlike the conventional p–q representation used by manufacturers, European transmission system operators now define reactive power requirements in the q–v plane. The method reflects this shift by computing and displaying reactive limits in the q–v plane to ensure compliance. The approach is validated with a field test of a 213 MVA hydropower plant, and a simulation test of a 450 MVA single-shaft combined-cycle gas turbine, with sensitivity analyses exploring the impact of key parameters on q–v compliance. Time-domain simulations demonstrate how reactive power limits evolve dynamically in response to changing operating conditions, supporting more accurate and robust voltage control in real time.

title: Transfer Learning for Data-Efficient Magnetic Core Loss Modeling in Electrical Machines via Parametric Homogenization and Neural Networks
abstract: Despite the urgent demand in industry, there do not yet exist practical and accurate simulation methods for calculating the magnetic losses of ferromagnetic laminated cores in electrical machine (EM) simulations. Transfer learning, a machine learning technique, utilizes a model developed for one task as a starting point for developing a model for another task. This study innovatively integrates parametric homogenized material laws with deep learning (DL) approaches. Firstly, the intrinsic resistance parameters characterizing core material properties are investigated through the combined application of the Bertotti model and an improved equivalent circuit model. Experimental data from prototypes are then used to visualize the influence patterns of different temperatures, harmonics, loads, and frequencies on these derived parameters. To both reduce the required data for improved performance and model the underlying mechanisms of mutual parameter impact, a sizeable auxiliary dataset was synthetically generated through the synergistic application of support vector machine, decision tree, and backpropagation (BP) neural network algorithms. By leveraging the pre-learned patterns of parameter variation, auxiliary data, and a small set of target data covering high-frequency, high-temperature, and high-load conditions, a two-stage feature transfer learning process is implemented using deep sparse autoencoder and BP neural network. Finally, comparative experiments are designed to verify the limitations of existing loss evaluation methods and to emphasize the importance of comprehensively considering multi-factor coupling effects in EM core loss modeling. The results demonstrate that the proposed local material law can serve as a conventional constitutive relationship in two-dimensional or three-dimensional modeling, and, when combined with DL algorithms, achieves a massive speed-up compared to monolithic coupling.

title: Radial Displacement Sensorless Control of Permanent Magnet Assisted Bearingless Synchronous Reluctance Motor in Full Speed Range
abstract: The displacement sensors utilized in the control system of the permanent magnet assisted bearingless synchronous reluctance motor (PMa-BSynRM) are associated with high cost and low reliability. To address this, this paper proposes a radial displacement sensorless control method in the full speed range. Firstly, the rotor suspension principle is expounded, and the voltage and current equations of the system are derived. Secondly, in the low speed range, the rotor displacement is estimated using high frequency square wave injection (HFSWI) combined with a phase-locked loop (PLL) for accurate signal demodulation. Thirdly, a left inverse observer is constructed using an improved radial basis function (RBF) neural network, and the initial parameters of the neural network are optimized by the weighted mean of vectors algorithm (INFO), ultimately achieving accurate displacement estimation. Furthermore, the transition boundaries between operational modes are determined through deceleration simulation, incorporating a weighted fusion algorithm to guarantee seamless switching across speed regions. Finally, the proposed approach is verified through simulation and comparative experiments. Experimental results demonstrate a maximum steady-state estimation error of 7 μm, while the settling time extends by only 11 ms under external disturbances. Overall, the proposed method exhibits superior estimation precision and robust disturbance rejection capability.

title: Research on Analytical Method of Parasitic Capacitance in Motor Windings Considering Impact of Distributed Disorder
abstract: The equivalent parasitic capacitance (Cp) of motor windings causes the voltage/current overshoot and ringing during the switching of wide-bandgap semiconductor devices. Therefore, it is necessary to model and calculate Cp to evaluate its impact on the switching devices. However, due to the winding deviations and spatial constraints of the slots, the arrangement of coils is disordered. Using the ideal single value of Cp may lead to the significant deviations in the evaluation of switching transients. To address the above issues, the analytical method of parasitic capacitance considering the impact of distributed disorder is studied in this paper. The impact of the winding model on the calculated value of Cp is investigated. The winding distribution patterns are categorized into three types: uniform, partially disordered, and fully disordered. An analytical method for the distributed capacitance is developed, incorporating the influence of random coil placement. A set of samples for the parasitic capacitance values of disordered windings is generated using a random sampling method. The sample distribution is determined through confidence intervals and the Chernoff bound to approximate the original distribution. The similarity between the two distributions is verified using the K-S test. The region with the highest frequency in the sample distribution is identified as the prediction interval for the winding’s parasitic capacitance value. Finally, the measurements are performed on the disordered distribution winding samples. The results prove the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed method.

title: Nonlinear Loss-Minimizing Control of Induction Motors With Inherent Constraint Satisfaction
abstract: In this paper, a novel nonlinear loss-minimizing control structure is proposed for induction motors that achieves field-oriented operation and minimization of the total copper and iron motor losses at the steady state, while inherently guaranteeing the required operating constraints (current and voltage). Opposed to the conventional loss-minimizing controllers that require the solution of a complex optimization problem and the continuous (online) update of the current reference values depending on the operating constraints, the proposed nonlinear loss-minimizing control (NLMC) introduces a novel structure that inherently limits the motor current and voltage inside the desired constraint set and requires the solution of a simplified optimization problem offline. Using nonlinear system theory (ultimate boundedness, vector field and invariant set theory), the boundedness of the motor currents and the entire constraint satisfaction are analytically proven for the proposed NLMC application, followed by a detailed closed-loop system stability analysis. In order to verify the theoretical contribution, the proposed NLMC is directly compared to the well-established field-oriented control and the conventional loss-minimizing control, using a digital Typhoon HIL real-time simulator and an experimental setup of a 1.5 kW Leroy Somer induction motor with varying speed reference and load torque values. Both the real-time simulation and the experimental procedure prove the NLMC capability of regulating the motor speed under speed reference values and torque load changes, while it achieves a minimum losses operation with inherent constraints satisfaction, by utilizing a simpler optimization problem.

title: A Novel Modified Logistic Function Based PV Source Modeling for PV Power Applications
abstract: In this paper, a novel modified logistic function-based explicit model for PV modules is proposed for accurate modeling of PV modules with minimal current-voltage (I<inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$-$</tex-math></inline-formula>V) curve data points. The proposed model requires only three I<inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$-$</tex-math></inline-formula>V coordinates: open circuit voltage, short circuit current, and maximum power points provided by the manufacturer or obtained experimentally. The shape parameters of the proposed model are calculated using a newly derived simplified expression based on hyperbolic identities. Therefore, the proposed model significantly reduces the computational complexity compared to the conventional benchmarks, such as implicit single diode and double diode models of PV module. The proposed model is validated for various PV modules of different cell types of technologies under different environmental conditions in terms of % error in maximum power point. The method eliminates the complex calculations, dependence on several PV parameters and the laboratory-based analysis of solar modules.

title: Battery Storage in More- and All-Electric Fishing Vessels: Real-Time Simulation and Experimental Verification
abstract: The transition of fuel-reliant fishing vessels to more- and all-electric alternatives is essential to reduce the fishing industry’s dependence on fuel. Most research on the energy transition in the maritime industry has focused on larger vessels. Larger vessels typically have multiple generation units; however, fishing vessels have fewer onboard resources, making control and operation more challenging. This paper introduces the development of a real-time simulation testbed for small fishing vessels using two Typhoon HIL 604 real-time simulators. Data obtained from an actual purse seine fishing vessel are applied in developing, validating, and benchmarking models for vessel dynamics, propeller behavior, and hydraulic performance. The models are adaptable and represent a 58-foot fishing vessel, including its propulsion system, hydraulic load, and battery storage capable of operating in both grid-forming and grid-following modes. The testbed is then used to examine integration of a battery energy storage system (BESS): during transit, during fishing operations, and during both transit and fishing operations. The results demonstrate the distinct benefits of both small and large battery installations on fishing vessels, including shorter travel time between the harbor and fishing grounds, stable voltage and frequency across operating modes, and reduced noise during fishing operations.

title: Andronov-Hopf Oscillator-Based Harmonic Elimination Scheme for Grid-Connected Inverters
abstract: Conventional harmonic elimination methods for Grid-Connected Inverters (GCI) rely on individual harmonic extraction and compensation, resulting in increased complexity and slow dynamic response. In this paper, the Virtual Oscillator based Harmonic Compensation (VO-HC) is proposed. It uses the Andronov–Hopf oscillator not for synchronization or grid-forming purposes, but to extract the fundamental component from the distorted grid current. The Hopf oscillator is inherently frequency-adaptive, allowing it to extract the fundamental component and attenuate harmonics with negligible phase delay compared to traditional filters. The extractor provides unity-gain fundamental tracking even under frequency deviations and weak-grid conditions. The extracted fundamental is then subtracted from the measured grid current to isolate the grid current harmonics. These harmonics are compensated using a simple proportional compensator loop in the stationary frame as a feedforward, operating in parallel with a conventional Synchronous Reference Frame (SRF) current controller. This results in fast low-order harmonic compensation of grid current, improving the Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) of the GCI system. Experimental results demonstrate THD reduction from up to 18.4% to below 2.5%, with a transient settling time of approximately 2–3 ms. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through both simulation and experimental results conducted on a laboratory two-inverter microgrid setup under distorted and weak-grid conditions.

title: Analysis and Calculation of the Control Winding Current During Crowbarless Asymmetrical Low-Voltage Ride-Through for Brushless Doubly-Fed Induction Generators
abstract: The present control winding (CW) current calculations are inaccurate due to the incomplete consideration of the output limitation of the machine side converter (MSC) during the crowbarless asymmetrical low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) of the brushless doubly-fed induction generator (BDFIG). Furthermore, there is a paucity of literature on the relationship between the peak CW currents and the time of the fault occurrence, which has a distinct impact on the analysis and evaluation of the effectiveness of the BDFIG LVRT control strategy. To address this challenge, this paper considers the transient process in the MSC, provides an innovative approximate expression for the CW flux linkage in SVPWM overmodulation, and derives an expression for the CW transient current considering the time of fault occurrence for the first time. From the expression, the CW current of the BDFIG prototype was calculated when the fault occurs at different moments. The calculation results indicate that the peak value of CW is closely related to the time of the fault occurrence and the maximum peak value of the CW current is more than twice the minimum peak value when the fault occurs at different times. Extensive simulation and experimental results under different asymmetrical short-circuit fault have validated the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed expression.

title: Improved Fast Terminal Sliding Mode Control With Disturbance Observer for Five-Phase Fault-Tolerant IPM Motor Drives
abstract: This paper presents a composite control strategy for five-phase fault-tolerant fractional-slot concentrated winding interior permanent magnet (FTFSCW-IPM) motor drives, aiming to alleviate the long-standing trade-off between fast dynamic response, chattering suppression, and disturbance rejection in sliding mode control. A variable exponential fast terminal reaching law with a continuous switching function is developed to explicitly shape the reaching dynamics, enabling rapid convergence when the system state is far from the sliding surface while ensuring smooth behavior near the surface. To further enhance robustness against load torque disturbances, a Luenberger torque disturbance observer (LTDO) with a slightly enhanced correction structure is incorporated as a feedforward compensation channel, thereby decoupling disturbance rejection from the sliding-mode switching gain design. In addition, a systematic comparative study involving four representative control schemes is conducted to clearly distinguish the individual and combined effects of the fast terminal sliding mode structure and the disturbance observer. Both simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed strategy achieves excellent speed tracking performance and improved disturbance rejection under sudden load torque variations.

title: Centralized Multi-Functional Power Management of an Integrated Microgrid–Electric Vehicle Charging Station
abstract: Various power management systems for microgrids (MGs) integrated with electric vehicle (EV) charging stations (CSs) have been designed so far, each addressing different aspects of grid-connected or off-grid operation. However, no previous research has developed multi-objective power management schemes that encompass all possible operating modes, including MG operation with the grid (G) without CS, CS operation with G without MG, MG-CS integrated operation with G, MG and CS autonomous operation in off-grid mode, and the interaction between MG and CS without G. In this article, innovative multi-functional power management strategies utilizing centralized control system have been modeled and designed for the aforementioned operational modes and simulated in the time-domain nonlinear environment of the MATLAB-SIMULINK. The results indicate the effective performance of different schemes in various operational states.

title: Temporal and spatial separations between spin glass and short-range order
abstract: Broken-symmetry-induced order parameters account for many phenomena in condensed matter physics. For spin glasses, such a framework dictates its theoretical construction, whereas experiments have only established dynamical behaviors such as frequency dependent magnetic susceptibility and aging but not the thermodynamic phase. Experimental techniques have limitations when the spin glass is probed as an isolated state. To resolve this conundrum, we create an evolution from long-range order using a well-controlled tuning of the disorder on a spinel's sublattice. Cross-referencing a series of specimens at both long (milliseconds to seconds) and short (picosecond) time scales illustrates the relationship between spin glass and long- and short-range orders. The dynamics of short- and long-range order formations are not affected by disorder, as revealed by neutron magnetic diffuse scattering, however the ranges of these orderings are changed by the introduced disorder. Across all specimens, the inflection point of the correlation length's temperature dependence fully matches with the peak in heat capacity, while spin glass can freeze either below or well above this characteristic temperature of spin order formation. Our results identify an uncorrelated coexistence of the two and attribute components of the spin glass to individual spins at domain walls between spin clusters.

title: Nanometric layered coating assembly bridging across micro-electronics and mega-voltage power grids
abstract: Electrical insulation remains a universal and critical challenge across electronic and electrical systems, from micro-electronics to mega-volt power grids. Many insulation failures originate from adverse interfacial processes, including carrier injection, surface flashover, and discharge erosion. This article highlights a scalable, technologically viable, and unified surface engineering solution based on conformal, self-assembled 2D nanocoating, which provide multifunctional barrier protection under extreme electrical, environmental, and thermal stresses. We envision this self-assembled nanocoating as a holistic dielectric surface re-engineering approach, enabling the next generation of electrification technologies.

title: Sharding-Based Asynchronous Coordination for Secure and Scalable Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading Under Delays and Attacks
abstract: The proliferation of distributed energy resources has enabled the emergence of prosumers and peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading. However, many existing decentralized market clearing schemes that require iterative message exchanges are vulnerable to false data injection (FDI) and can stall under heterogeneous communication delays. Blockchain solutions enhance integrity but often rely on synchronous optimization and global consensus, yielding excessive overhead. In this paper, a sharding-based asynchronous coordination mechanism for network-constrained P2P energy trading is developed. First, an asynchronous decentralized optimization method is developed to clear the market with respect to network constraints. Second, a dynamic sharding method is proposed to partition prosumers into low-latency shards by jointly considering trading relationships and communication delays, thereby localizing coordination and reducing cross-network synchronization. Third, a lightweight consensus mechanism that integrates asynchronous updates with a chained verification structure is designed to verify message correctness and detect malicious behaviors, thereby enabling fast intrashard agreement without the need for global synchronous rounds. Case studies demonstrate that the proposed approach preserves scalability and reduces the overall runtime by 79.15% compared with benchmark mechanisms while maintaining secure clearing performance under attack scenarios.

title: Future Trajectory Representation-Aided DRL for Real-Time Battery Energy Storage Dispatch in Distribution Networks
abstract: Dispatching battery energy storage systems (BESS) in distributed grids is challenging due to the sequential nature of the decision-making process, which needs to account for future uncertainties in system states and time-coupling constraints. Numerous forecasting techniques have been developed to capture such uncertainties, but most prioritize accuracy alone, and their potential for enhancing optimization performance has rarely been studied. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a novel forecasting-aided deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based BESS dispatch approach that incorporates future trajectory representation into the DRL state space to facilitate more proactive decisions. Specifically, an error-free representation network is first trained offline using self-supervised contrastive learning to encode upcoming electricity prices, load demand, and renewable generation trajectories. It explicitly disentangles trend and seasonal patterns using a mixture of autoregressive experts and a learnable Fourier layer. During online control, the DRL agent receives both the current system state and the learned forecast representation, which are fused using a dynamic routing attention mechanism that adaptively balances present versus future information. The trajectory contrastive learning allows the proposed method to better capture the temporal dynamics of stochastic variables and generate representations that are easier for the agent to exploit. By incorporating structured predictive representations into the control loop, the proposed method can make more forward-looking charging and discharging decisions that consider future uncertainties. Extensive simulations on the IEEE 34-node and 123-node test systems demonstrate that the proposed method yields more cost-efficient BESS control policies compared to baseline approaches.

title: Optimal PV Power Smoothing in Hydrogen-Battery Systems Using an Adaptive Equivalent Consumption Minimization Strategy
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) power plant variability presents a significant obstacle to grid stability. Hybrid energy storage systems (HESSs), which integrate battery energy storage systems (BESSs) with hydrogen units (i.e., electrolyzers and fuel cells), offer a viable solution to mitigate PV fluctuations and minimize power curtailment. However, existing control strategies are typically rule-based or offline-optimized, lacking the capability to address critical real-time challenges such as nonlinear efficiency characteristics, response delays in hydrogen subsystems, excessive hydrogen consumption, and battery degradation while complying with grid codes. This paper introduces an adaptive Equivalent Consumption Minimization Strategy (ECMS) for real-time, optimal power sharing among hydrogen-BESS systems. The controller minimizes a composite cost function that integrates efficiency-aware dispatch using empirical efficiency curves, health-aware penalties for aggressive state-of-charge (SOC) reversals and hydrogen overuse, delay-resilient compensation for hydrogen subsystem response lags, and degradation-aware control via online BESS aging assessment. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed strategy significantly improves ramp rate (RR) compliance and system longevity. Compared to benchmark techniques, the ECMS reduces BESS degradation by 50% and nearly eliminates RR violations while maintaining hydrogen demand satisfaction and ensuring smooth SOC recovery.

title: B-DRNet: A Stereo Vision-Based Framework for Safety Distance Monitoring in Substations
abstract: Monitoring the safety distance between maintenance personnel and live components is crucial for ensuring the safe and stable operation of the intelligent power grid. To address this issue, this study proposes a distance measurement framework, B-DRNet, which integrates keypoint detection with binocular stereo perception. The method constructs an innovative detector architecture incorporating three improvements: hierarchical feature aggregation block (HFAB), multi-scale attention hypergraph (MSAH), and a decoupled detection head (DDH), which significantly enhance feature representation capability and improve the detection accuracy of small objects. Meanwhile, a stereo perception module based on GwcNet is employed to obtain dense depth information, and coordinate mapping is utilized to achieve three-dimensional distance measurement. Experimental validation demonstrates that the proposed detector outperforms existing models in both detection performance and operational efficiency, with AP improved by 6.68%, frame rate reaching 333 f/s, and parameter size reduced to 1.05 M. The average distance measurement error is 3.18%, which meets practical application requirements and fully verifies its practicality and reliability in substation safety monitoring. B-DRNet achieves a favorable balance among detection accuracy, operational efficiency, and ranging reliability, enabling stable and accurate three-dimensional safety-distance monitoring in complex substation scenarios and providing an efficient solution for automated safety monitoring in substations.

title: Unified Load Flow Modeling and Boundary-Aware RoPINN Framework for Particle-Like EV Aggregation Dynamics
abstract: Accurate modeling of electric vehicle (EV) charging dynamics is essential for optimizing charging infrastructure and grid integration, especially when dealing with sparse data and random charging behavior. This paper proposes a unified load flow (ULF) model that captures the spatio-temporal evolution of charging behavior, incorporating EV arrival and departure dynamics as boundary conditions. A classical point optimization physics-informed neural network (PoPINN) is used to solve the ULF model, with a novel boundary condition design that ensures physical consistency during training. To enhance model consistency and robustness under stochastic and data-sparse conditions, a boundary-aware region-optimized PINN (RoPINN) is developed. This approach incorporates boundary information into regional optimization, enforcing arrival–departure consistency within local spatiotemporal regions and enabling reliable learning from incomplete data. The proposed framework provides a coherent data–physics integration strategy for modeling uncertain and incomplete EV charging information, enabling accurate prediction of charging power and load flow evolution. Simulation results on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate the robustness, accuracy, and practical applicability of the proposed method for large-scale EV charging optimization and smart grid management.

title: Explainable Optimal Vehicle Charging Strategy in Power Distribution Networks via Tree-Based Transportation Network Surrogates
abstract: The rapid adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) is driving increased charging demand, intensifying the interdependence between power distribution and transportation networks (PTNs). The main challenge in coordinating the EV routing and charging management within the PTN lies in the intractable nonlinear relationship between electricity price signals in the power distribution network (PN) and EV charging and routing behaviors in the transportation network (TN). Therefore, this paper proposes a novel constraint learning approach using XGBoost to solve the nontrivial bilevel optimization problem of vehicle charging within the PTN. XGBoost is first employed to capture the complex relationship between charging prices and optimal charging demand, leveraging its strong approximation capability to construct a tree-based surrogate model that approximates the TN decision model. Then the trained surrogate model is equivalently reformulated as mixed−integer linear programming (MILP) constraints and integrated into the vehicle charging optimization framework. Shapley values are further used to analyze the explainability of the tree-based surrogate model. Based on the constraint learning, a data-driven hybrid optimization model is developed for vehicle charging. Case studies validate the approximation accuracy and explainability of the tree-based surrogate model, as well as the effectiveness of the optimal strategy within the PTN.

title: LLM-Enhanced Offline Meta-Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Task V2G Regulation: A Human-AI Collaborative Framework
abstract: The rapid proliferation of electric vehicles (EVs) presents substantial challenges to effective charging and discharging regulation within distribution networks, particularly under increasingly diverse and dynamic regulatory scenarios. Conventional reinforcement learning (RL) methods, typically limited by task-specific training, struggle to generalize effectively across varying regulatory objectives and heterogeneous spatial EV distributions. To address these limitations, this study proposes a novel offline meta-reinforcement learning (Meta-RL) framework designed to enhance the adaptability of policy networks through a dedicated meta-network for task-specific identification. Specifically, we propose an innovative meta-network enhanced by large language models (LLMs), which simultaneously captures dynamic physical trajectories derived from historical operational data and encodes expert dispatch knowledge extracted from textual instructions. By integrating these physical and semantic modalities, the meta-network effectively generates task-specific embeddings, enabling the downstream policy network to rapidly adapt and formulate context-aware regulatory strategies. Comparative experiments demonstrate that the proposed offline Meta-RL framework achieves a 47.2% average reduction in operation cost compared to conventional single-task RL methods. Ablation studies further confirm that integrating physical and semantic information significantly improves task recognition accuracy and decision-making quality, reducing adaptation time by 68.8% and average operation costs by 18.4%.

title: Large Language Model-Based Smart Agents for Attack-Defense Game on Cyber-Physical Power Systems
abstract: With the deep integration of information technology, cyber-physical power systems (CPPSs) face increasingly complex attack-defense challenges. Traditional game theory-based methods struggle with sophisticated strategy reasoning and decision interpretability. This paper proposes an innovative CPPS attack-defense game paradigm incorporating large language model (LLM)-based smart agents to address these limitations. First, we define a game model integrating Bayesian Nash Equilibrium and betweenness centrality to characterize the strategy stability and key node prioritization. Second, we design smart agent architectures with memory, toolset, planning, and action execution modules to enable adaptive strategy formulation in complex environments. Then, we give a systematic elaboration of the dynamic game processes, including vulnerability scanning, attack, detection, response, and post-analysis phases. Experiments on IEEE 14 and IEEE 33 bus systems demonstrate that the proposed method significantly enhances defense success rate, convergence efficiency, and strategy diversity, validating the potential of LLMs in improving CPPS security through the intelligent attack-defense game.

title: Adaptive Fast Clearing Algorithm-Based Peer-to-Peer Transaction for Microgrid-Integrated Distribution Network Considering Uncertainty
abstract: Peer-to-peer (P2P) transaction has become an effective way to improve the economic efficiency of microgrids (MGs). However, existing studies neglect the impacts of electricity power-carbon-green certificate join cost (PCGC), energy-reserve co-optimization and uncertainty within MG on P2P transactions schemes. To fill this gap, this paper proposes a P2P transaction framework for interconnected MG, where carbon allowance-green certificate constraints, reserve constraints, joint chance constraints are employed respectively to capture PCGC coupling, reserve provisioning, and uncertainty impacts. An optimization-based piecewise-linear marginal utility function (MUF) is developed to characterize MG’s price-responsive behaviors under multi-resource coordination. Furthermore, an adaptive fast clearing algorithm (AFCA) is designed with a network-fee-exempt non-iterative clearing scheme and a network-fee-incorporated oscillation-resistant iterative scheme to ensure computational efficiency and distribution network security. Numerical results demonstrate that the MUF effectively captures the impacts of internal reserve, network constraints, risk preference, and PCGC on inter-MG P2P trading behaviors. The AFCA significantly accelerates computation, with a 97.72% time reduction compared to the widely used alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) in a 5-MG system, and solves the 20-MG system in only 1.45 s with an optimality error of merely 0.59%.

title: Data-Driven Modeling of High-Resolution Residential Load Profiles Using Low-Resolution Smart Meter Measurements
abstract: Accurate and high-resolution residential load profiles are essential for power system modeling, demand response planning, and effective grid operation. As the energy sector moves towards a more actively managed distribution system, the ability to understand residential energy consumption at a minute-by-minute scale becomes increasingly critical. High-resolution load profiles provide key insights into demand patterns and user behavior, enabling grid operators to design more effective energy solutions; however, residential load measurements in the field are typically recorded at low resolutions, such as 15-60 minutes, which makes it hard to study the characteristics of different residential customers. This paper addresses these challenges by introducing a data-driven approach to generate realistic, high-resolution residential load profiles based on low-resolution measurements and weather information. The proposed method retains the key features of the actual residential load measurements while offering appliance-level energy consumption details for each residential building. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed load profile generator, proving its capability to support utilities in optimizing residential energy management and ensuring a more reliable and resilient grid.

title: Optimal Power Allocation Strategy for Hydrogen Production System of ALK-PEM Electrolyzer Considering Second-Level Response Characteristics
abstract: Most electrolyzer scheduling models operate at minute-to-hour resolutions and thus overlook the second-level dynamics required to track fast renewable fluctuations, leading to avoidable wind curtailment and revenue loss for off-grid wind-to-hydrogen systems. This paper proposes an optimal power allocation framework for a hybrid electrolyzer system composed of alkaline (ALK) and proton exchange membrane (PEM). ALK provides low-cost, large-capacity baseline production but responds slowly, whereas PEM delivers second-level agility to absorb high-frequency power variations. A two-stage strategy is designed to couple efficiency-oriented power allocation with refined power dynamic regulation under explicit start/stop, ramp-rate, and capacity constraints. Moreover, a dual-layer array-rotation mechanism is incorporated to balance operating stress across stacks and prevent unit-specific overuse. Case studies using measured data from a practical project in Northeast China show that, compared with traditional power allocation methods, the proposed method increases hydrogen production by 3.3%-5.6%, reduces wind curtailment by 70.6%-94.7%, and improves hydrogen revenue by 21.9%-32.0%, enhancing renewable utilization and profitability.

title: Revisiting Angle Stability in Power Systems With Grid-Forming Power Converters
abstract: This letter presents a comprehensive analysis of the stability phenomenon related to the ability of generators to remain in synchronism when subjected to small or large disturbances, in power systems with both synchronous machines and grid-forming voltage source converters (GFM-VSC). This phenomenon is associated with two stability classes in the IEEE/PES classification, namely, rotor-angle stability (when involving synchronous machines) and slow-interaction converter-driven stability (when involving power converters). However, this work shows that this phenomenon is fully characterised with the slow dynamics of the angle difference between the voltage sources connected to the power system, regardless of whether they are synchronous machines (with rotors) or GFM-VSCs. Therefore, we suggest using the term angle stability to refer to this phenomenon, while slow-interaction converter-driven stability should only include slow interactions of different nature involving power converters.

title: Long‐Term Bio‐Spin Readouts Enable Decoding Immune‐Imposed Stress at the Single‐Cell Level
abstract: ABSTRACT Electronic spin dynamics represent a fundamentally important yet largely unexplored state parameter of living cells, offering stable sensitivity to intracellular paramagnetic environments associated with cellular stress responses. However, how immune‐imposed intracellular stress evolves over time and relates to divergent single‐cell outcomes remains unclear, owing to the lack of continuous and nonconsumptive readouts. Here, we establish a long‐term bio‐spin readout based on nanodiamonds hosting nitrogen‐vacancy centers as inheritable intracellular spin reporters, enabling continuous spin relaxometry in living cells. By integrating population‐level ROS‐associated paramagnetic stress profiling with long‐term single‐cell tracking in Hela and A549 cancer cells during coculture with activated macrophages, we identify three characteristic oxidative‐stress trajectory patterns—remote immune stress, immune evasion, and apoptosis—whose distinct temporal dynamics cannot be resolved by endpoint assays alone. Longitudinal bio‐spin measurements reveal that immune pressure is encoded not only by instantaneous oxidative levels but also by the temporal accumulation and regulation of intracellular stress. An empirical bio‐spin transition range provides an operational reference for distinguishing recoverable stress responses from apoptosis‐associated trajectories, while characteristic completion times capture the interaction‐ and cell‐type‐dependent kinetics of stress evolution. Together, this work establishes bio‐spin dynamics for resolving immune‐imposed stress histories and their associations with divergent cellular outcomes in living systems.

title: Early Warning of Extreme Weather-Induced N-$k$ Contingencies Leveraging Spatio-Temporal Analysis of Historical Event Sequences
abstract: Traditional N–<inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\bm {k}$</tex-math></inline-formula> contingency analysis is insufficient for addressing the growing threat of extreme weather to power system reliability and resilience. Existing methods for contingency construction and screening often fail to adequately consider power outage patterns involving simultaneous failures of multiple components caused by disastrous weather, limiting their applicability to high-impact low-probability events. Meanwhile, reliance on short-term weather forecasts makes these methods difficult to leave enough time for implementing preventive measures. To address these limitations, an early-warning framework leveraging spatio-temporal point process modeling of historical failure event sequences is proposed for extreme weather–induced N–<inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\bm {k}$</tex-math></inline-formula> contingencies. The core component is a Constrained Diffusion Spatio-Temporal Point Process (CDSTPP) model, which learns failure occurrence patterns under spatial, temporal, meteorological, and network constraints, enabling probabilistic forecasts of future line failures. Based on these forecasts, a contingency generation scheme synthesizes high-risk N–<inline-formula><tex-math notation="LaTeX">$\bm {k}$</tex-math></inline-formula> scenarios via sampling from predicted failure distributions to support preventive operation and anti-risk planning. Given the limited availability of high-resolution historical failure event data, a data augmentation approach that integrates meteorological reanalysis data with line fragility modeling is also proposed. The proposed framework is evaluated on the large-scale ENTSO-E test system. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in forecasting critical contingencies induced by extreme weather events and supporting proactive and resilient operational decision-making to mitigate blackout risks.

title: One catalyst, two geometries: Iridium catalysis enables stereodivergent synthesis of chiral Z- and E-allylated isochromanones
abstract: Alkene geometry strongly influences molecular structure and function, yet methods that provide stereodivergent access to both E - and Z -configured chiral building blocks remain rare. In an upcoming issue of Chem Catalysis , You and co-workers combine contra-thermodynamic alkene isomerization with iridium-catalyzed asymmetric allylic substitution to access either E - or Z -allylated 3-isochromanones with high regio- and enantioselectivity.

title: Adaptive Induced‐Fit via Engineered Linker Regioisomerization in Biomimetic Zeolitic Imidazolate Frameworks for Boosting SF 6 /N 2 Separation
abstract: ABSTRACT Capturing and recovering sulfur hexafluoride (SF 6 ) is a crucial yet formidable challenge in mitigating global warming. Herein, we propose a programmable linker regioisomerization strategy within zeolitic imidazolate frameworks (ZIFs) to modulate their stimulus‐responsive structural flexibility, thereby significantly enhancing SF 6 capture efficiency from nitrogen (N 2 ) streams. Simultaneous regioisomerization of the methyl group in ZIF‐8 and the aldehyde group in ZIF‐90 on the imidazolate linkers yields ZIF‐94, which exhibits a rare guest‐induced reversible framework deformation upon SF 6 adsorption. This behavior confers an enzyme‐like induced‐fit recognition mechanism for SF 6 molecules, strengthening host–guest interactions. As a result, ZIF‐94 achieves a high SF 6 adsorption capacity of 1.97 mmol g −1 and an ultrahigh SF 6 stacking density of 1438.69 mg cm −3 at 298 K and 0.1 bar, along with dramatically enhanced SF 6 /N 2 selectivities over ZIF‐8 and ZIF‐90. In situ experiments and theoretical analyses reveal that the SF 6 ‐induced structural flexibility of ZIF‐94 allows the framework to dynamically adjust and optimize its cage structure to match gas molecules, thus leading to significantly reinforced SF 6 /N 2 separation performance. The experimental column breakthrough tests and pressure swing adsorption simulations confirm the practical separation performance for SF 6 /N 2 mixtures in ZIF‐94. This work offers useful insights for designing flexible adsorbents for gas separation applications.

title: Space‐Confined Water Isotope Transport in Conductive MOF Thin Film
abstract: ABSTRACT The century‐old challenge of isotope separation might be addressed by conductive metal–organic framework (cMOF) thin films featuring ordered nanopores, designable charge‐transport pathways, and potential flexibility. However, resolving and amplifying the microscopic kinetic differences between water isotopologues within such confined spaces remains nontrivial. In this work, proton‐ and electron‐coupled two‐dimensional π‐conjugated cMOF thin films (Cu 1 TPB 0.1 − x C) are fabricated through controllable layer‐by‐layer growth with oriented narrow pores and flexibility. Correlating electrical‐ and mass‐transduced gas‐sensor technologies, the subtle differences in the interactions of H 2 O and D 2 O with the framework were identified, revealing a complex multistage mass transport. Comparison of cMOFs with different pore sizes shows that this identification originates from distinct conduction mechanisms. Notably, the Cu 1 TPB 0.1 − x C thin film with a strong space‐confined effect exhibits a complex multistage electrical response due to its unique proton–electron‐coupled conduction characteristics, thereby enabling further differentiation of the transport processes of H 2 O and D 2 O on the outer surface and within the confined spaces. The oriented cMOF films therefore provide a real‐time platform for resolving and amplifying subtle isotope‐dependent transport dynamics in confined pores, offering mechanistic guidance for the design of porous materials with controlled water‐isotopologue transport.

title: Metal Oxides Catalyze Formation of Dehydroamino Acids by Phosphate β‐Elimination Under Physiological Conditions
abstract: ABSTRACT The dehydroamino acids (DHAAs) dehydroalanine and dehydrobutyrine are formed in proteins posttranslationally from serine and threonine, respectively. They contain an electrophilic alkene, which reacts readily with nucleophiles by Michael addition, giving rise to a variety of chemical modifications as well as protein crosslinks. Recent work has shown DHAAs and their modifications to be highly prevalent in protein aggregates isolated from brains of Alzheimer's Disease (AD) patients. As there is no human enzyme known to catalyze the formation of DHAAs, this raised the question of how they are produced. We show here that metal oxides, particularly the iron oxides goethite and hematite, efficiently catalyze the formation of DHAAs in model phosphopeptides in vitro under physiologically relevant conditions. Iron oxides are known to accumulate in the human brain with age, and this deposition is enhanced in neurodegenerative disorders like AD. The DHAA formation by heterogeneous catalysis reported here provides a previously unknown mechanism linking iron deposition to protein crosslinking in AD and potentially other neurodegenerative diseases where iron accumulation and protein aggregation co‐occur.

title: Distributed Location Method for SPG Faults in Distribution Networks Combining Zero-Sequence and Phase-to-Phase Current Fault Components
abstract: Reliable distributed localization of single-phase-to-ground (SPG) faults is becoming increasingly critical as modern active distribution networks demand faster restoration and minimized outage impact. However, SPG fault currents are typically weak, highly distorted by arcs, and easily contaminated by noise, making single-source localization methods inherently unreliable. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a distributed localization framework that jointly exploits zero-sequence components (ZSCs) and phase-to-phase current fault components (PPCFCs). The intrinsic behaviors of both source signals are first examined considering transient attenuation, triggering delays, and measurement errors, revealing fundamental limitations that cannot be resolved by improved feature extraction or classification alone. Building upon these findings, a multi-source fusion-based distributed method is developed, where ZSCs- or PPCFCs-based source indicators are selectively activated only when their reliability is ensured, and one compensates for the other under degraded conditions. This cooperative decision mechanism substantially enhances both faulty-feeder identification and fault-section localization. The method requires only local measurements for feeder-level detection and uses simple binary communication between adjacent terminals for section-level location, ensuring scalability and practical deployment. Extensive tests across diverse fault scenarios confirm its strong robustness and high localization accuracy.

title: Simplicial Graph-Based Detection and Localization of Cyber Attacks Against Large-Scale Smart Grids
abstract: Ensuring the resilience of large-scale power systems against cyber attacks is critical to maintaining the stability of modern cyber-physical energy systems. Existing machine learning (ML)-based detection frameworks predominantly focus on pairwise node interactions (i.e., edges) and often overlook capturing higher-order topological structures (i.e., simplicial complexes) that emerge within power networks. This paper introduces a novel simplicial recurrent graph neural network (SRGNN) for attack detection and localization in large-scale smart grid infrastructure. Unlike conventional graph models, SRGNN incorporates higher-order simplicial interactions to capture group-wise dependencies among buses and transmission lines, allowing the model to better reflect the multi-scale dynamics of grid operation and control. We investigate the robustness of our model against benchmark and proposed complex simplicial-based attack node selection strategies. Our extensive experiments on large-scale transmission power networks (<inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$2{,}869$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-bus, <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$9{,}241$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-bus, and <inline-formula> <tex-math notation="LaTeX">$70{,}000$ </tex-math></inline-formula>-bus systems) demonstrate that the proposed SRGNN model outperforms ML-based benchmark models, achieving superior detection and localization performance by 9–39% and 8–35%, respectively, in detection rate against complex attacks. These results underscore the importance of modeling higher-order topological structures for robust and scalable security in power systems.

title: Scalable Building HVAC Control Through Laxity-Based Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Demand flexibility is playing a vital role in maintaining grid power balance, reducing peak demand, and saving energy bills. Given their highly shiftable characteristics and significant contribution to a building’s energy consumption, Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) systems can provide valuable demand flexibility to the power systems by adjusting their power consumption in response to electricity price and power system needs. To exploit such flexibility in terms of both operation time and demand level, modeling and efficient aggregation techniques of HVAC load flexibility are investigated in this paper. To tackle the curse of dimensionality issue associated with an increasing number of HVAC devices, the notion of laxity for HVAC is proposed in this work to quantify the urgency level of each building’s operation request. Considering the inherent complexity and uncertainty presented in HVAC systems, we design a novel deep reinforcement learning (RL)-based controller to schedule the aggregate dispatched power based on the efficient representation of aggregated laxity information as well as the electricity price. For each HVAC load, only laxity information is revealed instead of full states, and integrated with proposed RL agent using least-laxity-first (LLF) rule for power allocation. To validate the superior efficiency and performance provided by our laxity-based RL agent, we evaluate the temperature control and the energy cost savings of a large number of HVACs in both single-zone and multi-zone scenarios under varying climate and electricity market conditions. Our data-driven approach also significantly saves the modeling and data burden compared to model-based controllers. Empirically, numerical results also indicate that the proposed approach outperforms standard RL with full HVAC states. Compared to the widely used deep RL baseline, it achieves up to 42% reduction in total energy cost while maintaining comparable average temperature deviation.

title: Coordinated Load Frequency Control for Multi-Frequency Oscillations in Wind-Pumped Storage Hybrid Microgrids
abstract: Hybrid microgrids (MGs), particularly those incorporating wind power and pumped storage, have been widely adopted for renewable energy generation. However, hydraulic characteristics of pumped storage units (PSUs) and inter-generator interactions induce inevitably multi-frequency oscillations during load frequency control (LFC). To capture these oscillation behaviors and achieve effective suppression, this paper proposes a coordinated LFC strategy for hybrid MGs that integrates high-fidelity system modeling. A novel distributed frequency response (DFR) model is developed that incorporates hydraulic states (e.g., pressure heads in complicated pipelines and surge tank water levels) and network topology, offering improved accuracy over conventional average system frequency (ASF) models. Based on this model, a multi-input multi-output model predictive control (MIMO-MPC) scheme is designed to track the power allocation setpoint and enable wind turbines to participate in LFC in coordination with synchronous generators. Simulation results on 6-bus and IEEE 39-bus systems demonstrate the proposed strategy’s superiority in frequency regulation. Under variable wind conditions, it reduces the integral of time-weighted absolute error (ITAE) of frequency deviation for the PSU by 47.3% compared to the PI control. These outcomes validate the enhanced transient performance and robustness of the scheme for practical smart grid applications.

title: Demand Response Potential Evaluation for Commercial HVAC Loads Considering Cooling Storage in Chilled Water Loops
abstract: Commercial HVAC systems offer great potential for demand response (DR). Existing methods for HVAC DR evaluation often neglect the cooling storage effect within chilled water loops. However, this effect provides substantial flexibility and its omission leads to considerable underestimation of DR potential.
